definition: A hierarchical control system (HCS) is a form of control system in which a set of devices and governing software is arranged in a hierarchical tree.
details: When the links in the tree are implemented by a computer network, then that hierarchical control system is also a form of networked control system.

explainer.lead: A hierarchical control system arranges a set of devices and governing software in a hierarchical tree. It matters for organizing control across many devices at different levels.

tiers.eli5: It's like a company: a boss sets goals, managers break them into tasks, and workers carry them out, all in a chain of command.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers structure controllers in levels so higher levels set objectives and lower levels execute them. A pitfall noted by the definition's context: when tree links run over a computer network, the system is also a networked control system, adding network dependence.
tiers.paperLevel: A hierarchical control system is a form of control system in which a set of devices and governing software is arranged in a hierarchical tree; when the links in the tree are implemented by a computer network, it is also a form of networked control system.

explainer.example: Governing software at the top of the tree issues commands that cascade down to devices at lower levels, with communication links between levels carried over a computer network.
